newsitem.title: JAPAN: Wrong for stocks to fall on reform worries -- EPA.
newsitem.headline: Wrong for stocks to fall on reform worries -- EPA.

text.p: It is wrong if stocks are falling on worries that the Japanese government will fail to push through deregulation, Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso told reporters on Friday.
"If stocks are falling on the belief that the government will not be able to carry out deregulation, then that view is wrong," Aso said.
Aso added that there appeared to be two ways to look at the recent fall in stock prices.
One view is that stocks are falling on the belief that deregulation will fail.
The other is that certain sectors are being sold as they may be hurt by the deregulation measures.
Aso said he could not assess the effect of deregulation, but added that the government was moving ahead with its financial reform plans on the view that they will revitalise the economy.
